headline: Bank of England Raises Interest Rate to 4.0% Over Inflation Risks
summary: The Bank of England increased its benchmark interest rate to 4.0% and warned that UK inflation could reach 5% in 2027, citing elevated global energy prices stemming from Middle East tensions.
why: The Bank of England's monetary decisions determine borrowing costs across the UK economy and impact Sterling exchange values.

impacts.name: UK 10-Year Gilt Yield
impacts.why: An interest rate hike to 4% lifts sovereign borrowing costs across the curve.

impacts.name: British Pound
impacts.why: Higher policy rates support yield differentials for Sterling against other currencies.
